Owning team, plan or programme

The headline claim

One sentence that would satisfy a reader who reads nothing else: what it does, for whom, and where it stops. Three lines maximum.

The one number
One line of status
As of DD Mon YYYY

How it works

01Step title, four words What happens, in about twenty-five words. Name the thing that would surprise a reader who assumed this step was trivial.
02Step title Keep step descriptions within a few words of each other: the row is as tall as its tallest cell, so one long step costs every column.
03Step title Describe the mechanism, not the intent. "Routes on what the caller said" beats "intelligently understands the request".
04Step title The last step is usually what happens when the thing cannot finish, and what gets recorded. Both matter more to a leader than the happy path.

How it is set up

Configuration area
Plain words first, then the live identifier in monospace where a reader might want to verify it. Explain what the setting buys, not what it is called.
Second area
Seven to nine rows is the working range. Fewer reads thin; more and the column runs past its neighbour.
Third area
Where a setting exists because something went wrong once, say so in a clause. That clause is usually the most credible line on the page.

What it does, and what you can see

Group one

  • Leads with a verb phrase and finishes in one sentence of about twenty words.
  • Names a guarantee rather than a capability wherever there is one: what it will not do is more informative than what it can.

Group two

  • Names the surface and then what question it answers. A reader should be able to tell which one to open without being told how it is built.
  • Covers every surface that exists. A one-pager that omits one is a one-pager somebody has to correct in the room.

What this buys you

A benefit as a claim
Two sentences. The first states the consequence, the second says why it holds.
Second benefit
Keep all four within a couple of words of each other. The row is as tall as its tallest cell.
Third benefit
If a benefit needs a number to be true and the number does not exist yet, it belongs in the note instead.
Fourth benefit
The weakest of the four is the one to cut when the page does not fit.

Where this stands. The honest paragraph: what is live, what the data really is, when it started, and what this page does not claim. Writing it well is what keeps the rest of the page credible.
